answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each identity to publish a distinct, checkable artifact whose cost is dominated by sequential human-style judgement rather than compute. An agent files a sonnet-like essay on a freshly drawn prompt, and a quartz-sealed registry records the prompt, the author key, and the deadline. A willow of cloned accounts cannot share one submission because prompts are unique per identity per epoch, and reuse is detected at intake by comparing committed prompt hashes, so scale multiplies unpaid writing and review time.
